issues.span: one should bear it in mind
issues.evidence: དེ་བཞིན་གནོས (mnos) is "undertake/take on likewise"; bo-kunpal 5-32 glosses དེ་བཞིན་དུ་མནོས་ཏེ་གནས་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག ("having so undertaken, remain"), Sanskrit tathā tiṣṭhet "remain thus". "Bear it in mind" adds an object ("it") and drops the དེ་བཞིན "thus/likewise" that links back to the shame, respect and fear.
issues.fix: one should thus take it on and remain so

issues.evidence: ཤིང་བཞིན་ is rendered "like a log of wood" in the glossary and in 5-48, 5-50, 5-51; here the same phrase ཤིང་བཞིན་དུ་ཡང་ is rendered "like a piece of wood", an unmotivated inconsistency (bo-kunpal 5-34 likens it to a great tree stump unmoved by wind).

བྱ་བ་བསྡོགས་ནས is glossed by bo-shenga 5-39 as བརྩམས་པར་བྱས་ནས ("having begun/set about") and by bo-kunpal 5-39 as བྱ་བ་དེའི་མགོ་བརྩམས་པ ("having begun that action"); Sanskrit kriyām ākṣipya. The action is already started, not merely prepared for.
issues.fix: Having set about an action with the thought,

issues.span: Does not escape from how it is bound
issues.evidence: ཇི་ལྟར་བཏགས་པ་མི་འཆོར་བར། དེ་ལྟར་འབད་པ་ཀུན་གྱིས་བརྟག is a ji-ltar...de-ltar clause: as bound, it does not escape (bo-gyaltsab 5-40: ཇི་ལྟར་བཏགས་པ་མི་འཆོར་བར་). "Escape from how it is bound" is hard to parse and suggests escaping a manner of binding, not escaping the pillar.
issues.fix: So that the mad elephant of the mind, once tied to the great pillar of reflecting on the Dharma, does not escape

issues.evidence: བདེ་གཤེགས་བསླབ་པ has no plural marker; bo-gyaltsab 5-46 has བདེ་གཤེགས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པ and bo-shenga བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པའི་བསླབ་པ (singular); Sanskrit tāthāgatīṃ śikṣām is singular.
